headline: EQUINOX GOLD + ORLA MINING COURT ORDER TOMORROW — CLOSES JULY 31, CREATING CANADA'S LARGEST NEW GOLD PRODUCER OF 2026
snippet: Equinox Gold and Orla Mining secured near-unanimous shareholder approval on July 22 — 99.91% of Orla votes in favour — and now await the Supreme Court of British Columbia's final order expected July 28 before closing on July 31, 2026. The combination, with former Orla shareholders owning ~33% and Equinox ~67%, unites Orla's Camino Rojo heap-leach mine in Zacatecas with Equinox's multi-mine Americas portfolio including Greenstone, Fazenda, and RDM — the largest Canadian mid-tier gold consolidation of 2026.

headline: JAPAN SEABED MUD: 54% HEAVY RARE EARTHS CONFIRMED — FULL-SCALE MINING TRIAL SET 2027 AS BEIJING'S EXPORT BAN SQUEEZES DYSPROSIUM
snippet: Analysis of 50 tonnes of deep-sea mud recovered from 6km depth near Japan's Minamitorishima Island found that heavy and medium rare earth elements — including gadolinium, dysprosium, and terbium — account for 54% of total REE content, the exact heavy elements China restricted for export in April 2025. Japan plans a 350-tonne-per-day full-scale mining trial in early 2027 via JAMSTEC, but commercial production is at least a decade away, meaning the strategic signal is long-term while ex-China dysprosium and terbium prices remain 4-5x above pre-ban levels in the near term.

headline: COPPER WITHIN 2% OF US ALL-TIME RECORD: COMEX $6.55/LB, SHANGHAI STOCKS DOWN 82% SINCE MAY, YANGSHAN PREMIUM AT $103-109/T
snippet: Copper reached $6.55/lb on Comex — less than 2% from its US all-time record set in early June 2026 — as SHFE-deliverable copper inventories collapsed 82% since May and LME stocks fell 28%, with 56% of the remaining 296,625 tonnes sitting on cancelled warrants awaiting delivery. The Yangshan copper import premium surged to $103-109/tonne (highest since December 2023) and the Comex-LME spread widened to nearly $600/t, driven by tariff-positioning pulling US physical demand sharply above global spot, with satellite data showing 16% of global copper smelter capacity was inactive in Q2.

headline: ELEMENT 29 DRILLS 1,534m AT 0.58% CuEq AT ELIDA PORPHYRY PERU — LONGEST INTERCEPT IN PROGRAM HISTORY (TSXV: ECU)
snippet: Element 29 Resources (TSXV: ECU) released assay results from ELID035 — a 1,534.6-metre intercept grading 0.58% CuEq (0.34% Cu, 0.064% Mo, 2.56 g/t Ag) from 56.6m to end-of-hole at 1,591m, the longest intersection in the Elida Porphyry Cu-Mo-Ag program in central Peru. The hole extends below the existing inferred resource of 321.7 million tonnes at 0.32% Cu and confirms the porphyry system is open to depth, adding resource expansion optionality in a permissive Peruvian copper corridor at $6.30/lb copper.

headline: GERMANIUM +27.8%, DYSPROSIUM +25.4% IN JULY — CHINA BANS US RARE EARTH PRODUCERS FROM SUPPLY; NdPr HITS 2026 HIGH AT $112-115/KG
snippet: All 18 rare earth elements tracked rose in July 2026, led by germanium (+27.8%), indium (+26.5%), and dysprosium (+25.4%), with China's Rare Earth Price Index reaching 270.5 on July 24 and NdPr oxide climbing to ¥747-767/kg (~US$112-115/kg) — a new 2026 high. On June 22, China's MOFCOM added MP Materials and USA Rare Earth — the two leading US rare earth producers — to its export control list, prohibiting supply of China-origin feedstocks and pushing ex-China buyers into an already supply-constrained market now entering its second consecutive year of NdPr deficit.

headline: NEWMONT Q2 2026: $2.2B RECORD FREE CASH FLOW ON 1.29M OZ GOLD — $1.9B RETURNED TO SHAREHOLDERS AT $1,680/OZ AISC (NYSE: NEM)
snippet: Newmont Corporation (NYSE: NEM) reported Q2 2026 results on July 23 with record free cash flow of $2.2 billion and operating cash flow of $2.9 billion on 1.29 million attributable gold ounces at $1,680/oz all-in sustaining cost, returning approximately $1.9 billion to shareholders through dividends and buybacks. The company reaffirmed full-year guidance of 5.3 million attributable gold ounces and confirmed that Cadia, which had paused underground operations following an April seismic event, resumed production from both operating caves in mid-June with no full-year guidance impact.

headline: GROUP ELEVEN HITS 8.3% Zn+Pb IN 550m STEP-OUT FROM STONEPARK MRE — NEW ZONE IN IRELAND; CEO CALLS IT MOST SIGNIFICANT RESULT IN 9 YEARS (TSXV: ZNG)
snippet: Group Eleven Resources (TSXV: ZNG) drilled hole 26-2638-07 at its 78.62%-owned Stonepark Project in Ireland and returned 15 metres of new zinc-lead mineralization including 2.8 metres at 8.3% combined Zn+Pb (5.5% Zn, 2.9% Pb, with a 1.0m interval at 21.7% Zn+Pb and 4 g/t Ag) — in a step-out drilled 550 metres from the nearest edge of the existing Stonepark Mineral Resource Estimate in previously untested ground. CEO Bart Jaworski called it the most significant result at Stonepark since the company acquired the license block in 2017, adjacent to the PG West license hosting the high-grade Ballywire discovery.

headline: GOLD SPECS BEARISH 47.2% ENTERING FOMC WEEK — NET LONGS FALL 7,564 CONTRACTS; LIGHTEST POSITIONING SINCE LATE 2023
snippet: The CFTC Commitment of Traders report published July 24, 2026 shows gold large speculator net positions at 186,682 contracts — down 7,564 on the week — with the speculator strength score registering a bearish 47.2%, the lightest speculative positioning in gold futures in nearly three years. The reduction in speculative length heading into the July 28-29 FOMC meeting means the crowded-long positioning that helped fuel gold's January 2026 all-time high above $5,000 has largely been flushed, creating a setup where a Fed hold can re-attract speculative buyers rather than merely confirm an existing overweight.

headline: URANIUM HOLDS $86 AS AI HYPERSCALER NUCLEAR PPAS MULTIPLY AND KAZAKHSTAN SUPPLY REMAINS UNCERTAIN — UP 20% YEAR-OVER-YEAR
snippet: Uranium spot held at $86/lb as of July 24 — up 20% year-over-year — sustained by hyperscalers signing long-term nuclear power purchase agreements to secure baseload power for AI data centers, while Kazakhstan's operational challenges continue to constrain term contract deliveries. With Cameco Q2 earnings due July 31 (and Cigar Lake's two-week July curtailment to be disclosed) and the Section 232 uranium import review report still pending, uranium investors enter the final week of July with two simultaneous binary catalysts.

headline: GOLD SWOT JULY 2026: PRODUCERS DELIVER RECORD EARNINGS BUT EQUITIES STILL PRICING IN PROLONGED CORRECTION FROM $5,000 ATH
snippet: Sprott's weekly Gold SWOT analysis for late July 2026 highlights senior gold producer Q2 earnings as a sector strength — with DPM Metals delivering a solid production beat alongside Newmont's record $2.2B FCF — while flagging the market's persistent equity discount as the key weakness: gold miners (GDX down 12% YTD) are trading at historically wide discounts to spot gold despite record margins, as equity markets price in duration risk on the $4,051 current price against cost structures built for $3,000-3,500 gold during the 2023-2025 ramp. The divergence creates the asymmetric setup that has historically preceded sector re-ratings when gold price direction becomes clear.
